From an economic perspective, a clear shift by major central banks toward more accommodative monetary policy, coupled with elevated liquidity and concerns about the long-term purchasing power of fiat currencies, would boost demand for scarce digital assets.

Within the cryptocurrency space, continued growth in spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, broader institutional adoption, increasing corporate treasury allocations, and a sustained resurgence of risk appetite for digital assets would create a highly favorable liquidity environment, reinforcing Bitcoin’s status as the market’s primary reserve asset.

Under this highly speculative scenario, and assuming a full-blown crypto bull market returns alongside supportive external conditions, Bitcoin could reach between $850,000 and $1,500,000, with a stretch target toward $2,500,000+ by January 1, 2027.

#5369. Binance Reveals When It Will Resume Withdrawals After Historic Hack

Binance co-CEO Yi He has said the crypto exchange expects to restore withdrawal services within the next 48 hours.

"We're working on improving the withdrawal service and related address controls," she said.

According to Yi He, deposits are unaffected and are operating as usual.

However, Yi He didn't specify when withdrawal services would be fully restored.

This announcement was made after Binance temporarily paused deposits and withdrawals as it was looking into what appears to be the biggest crypto hack in history.

According to the crypto exchange, the estimated impact of the incident is around $6.3 billion. Crypto analytics firm Chainalysis has stated that the impact is around $6.4 billion.

Binance has already collaborated with blockchain partners to freeze about $3 billion of the affected funds.

Also, the crypto exchange has assured its customers that all losses will be covered by its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds.

Binance has also released preliminary findings on what could have led to the security breach.

The crypto exchange claims that it could be the compromise of one of its DevOps engineers' laptops.

According to the exchange, the compromised laptop enabled the hacker to access a service container from which unauthorized withdrawal transactions were initiated.

However, the crypto exchange has also mentioned that no leaked wallet private keys have been found so far during the investigation.

Binance has already revoked authorization for the compromised address. The exchange is also collaborating with law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence firms to trace the stolen funds.

Binance has also promised to share a detailed technical report once the investigation is over. Also, it will release an updated Proof of Reserves after the security enhancements are completed.

However, crypto analytics firm Chainalysis claims that the record-breaking attack could have been carried out by North Korean hackers.

According to Chainalysis, investigators found that crypto funds stolen in the Binance hack have been mixed with crypto associated with last month's Bitget exploit.

According to Chainalysis co-founder Jonathan Levin, TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group, could be the attacker.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs also has high confidence that TraderTraitor is behind the attack.

The North Korean hacking group has been associated with a number of big crypto thefts, such as the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

But Binance hasn't made any official statement yet about the attacker. Binance's investigation is still in progress.

#5367. Crypto Developers Using Claude Via VS Code May Have Been Compromised: This Version Has a Backdoor

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Developers using Claude AI through Visual Studio Code (VS Code) may have been exposed to a serious security threat after researchers discovered a malicious version of the popular coding assistant's extension.

According to an October 30 report from cybersecurity researchers at OpenSourceMalware, version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension contained a hidden backdoor that could enable attackers to remotely access infected computers.

The malicious version was identified in the Open VSX extension registry, where developers download tools for their coding environments.

The compromised extension reportedly looked and functioned like the legitimate Claude Code tool, making the threat particularly difficult to notice. However, researchers discovered additional malicious code designed to run automatically when the extension loaded.

Once activated, the backdoor attempted to establish a remote connection to an attacker-controlled server, potentially giving hackers access to the victim's computer.

More concerningly, the malware was designed to remain active even after the computer restarted.

This means simply closing VS Code or stopping work with Claude might not eliminate the threat.

Although the attack was not specifically designed to target cryptocurrency users, developers working on blockchain projects could face significant risks.

Their computers may contain sensitive information, including private keys, wallet credentials, exchange API keys, and access to cryptocurrency infrastructure.

If attackers successfully gained remote access, they could potentially obtain this information and use it to compromise wallets or projects.

However, researchers did not report confirmed cryptocurrency theft or identify any specific blockchain-related functionality in the malicious code.

The researchers confirmed malicious code in the analyzed Open VSX version but could not establish how it was introduced.

Importantly, the findings do not prove that Anthropic's official VS Code Marketplace release or its broader distribution systems were compromised.

Developers who installed version 2.1.313 through Open VSX should treat their systems as potentially compromised and investigate immediately.

Removing the extension alone may not be sufficient, as the backdoor was designed to persist independently.

The incidents have renewed concerns about the security of exchanges, wallets, and services connected to crypto applications.

A wave of attacks has also targeted older BTCPay Server installations and a vulnerable WordPress crypto-payment plugin, according to recent security reports.

Bitcoin also needs to show that the recent security incidents have not triggered a deeper withdrawal of capital from the industry. Binance’s outflows and the latest exchange breaches will remain important sentiment indicators.

For now, the Iran story is unfolding alongside a wider Bitcoin and crypto confidence test. If the sell-off continues, Bitcoin could face another challenge to its recovery. If geopolitical fears cool and the hacking fallout remains contained, buyers may get an opportunity to step back in.

The cryptocurrency market is going through the largest robbery in its history, but industry veterans manage to find a reason for harsh dark humor in it.

Former Ripple CTO and creator of the XRP Ledger network David Schwartz reacted to the Binance exchange hack with a caustic joke aimed at his main historical competitor, the Stellar (XLM) blockchain.

Schwartz commented on a post by EasyA co-founder Dom Kwok, who complained that hackers had wiped out his balances, leaving only Litecoin untouched. The former Ripple CTO, in turn, quipped: “These sick b*stards dropped an extra 517 XLM into my Binance account!”

The sarcasm is tied to a long-running corporate conflict: Stellar was created by former Ripple co-founder Jed McCaleb, and the idea that hackers forcibly “credit” victims with competitors’ tokens instantly went viral.

Despite Schwartz’s ironic tone, the blow landed directly on Ripple’s own ecosystem. The attackers instantly withdrew 233.46 million XRP tokens (about $296 million) from Binance’s hot wallets. It is impossible to return them: the XRP Ledger architecture excludes forced freezing of the native token at the protocol level.

However, with the company’s second asset, the situation turned out differently. Ripple Senior Vice President Jack McDonald announced that the company had detected the movement of stolen Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin and urgently blocked the attackers’ addresses.

Binance co-founder Yi He has already publicly thanked the Ripple team for promptly freezing about $200 million in RLUSD funds, emphasizing that user funds are now protected (SAFU). While XRP showed the hackers absolute decentralization, the controlled RLUSD stablecoin became the main protection tool.

The incident itself became part of the historic Binance hack totaling $6.3–6.36 billion across 10 blockchain networks.

At the moment, the exchange, together with partners, has managed to freeze a total of about $3 billion across various ecosystems, and according to blockchain sleuths, the North Korean cyber group TraderTraitor (Lazarus) is behind the attack itself.

The industry spent big to stop that. Crypto-linked groups have put more than $200 million into this cycle. Yet the bill they most wanted, the CLARITY Act, is still stuck in the Senate, seven weeks after a 49-50 vote left it 11 votes short.

Now the clock is the problem. Any bill that hasn’t passed when this Congress ends on January 3 dies with it, and the next Congress would have to start from scratch.

BTC USD price itself is down 1.3% in 24 hours and 9.8% over the past month, and it is sitting right on its 200-day average. Spot ETFs lost $398.6 million on Monday, and the Fear & Greed Index reads 26.

So how long could a Democratic Congress hold up crypto laws, and does the market care?

One law is done, the other is stalled. The GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law, was signed in July 2025, and Treasury says its rules are on track. The CLARITY Act never made it through the Senate. It would decide when a token falls under the SEC or the CFTC.

The House passed it 294-134 on July 17, 2025. The Senate Banking Committee advanced its version 15-9 in May. Then, on September 15, a vote to open debate failed 49-50 when it needed 60.

#5355. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable."

The coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest update on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

#5352. The Exchange Quote Looks Good — But What Will You Actually Receive? A Practical Look at Boomchange

Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

A crypto exchange quote can look attractive until you start asking how much money will actually reach your destination. You enter an amount, see an estimated return, and begin planning your next move. But is that figure guaranteed? When evaluating a service such as Boomchange, the final amount matters more than an impressive number on the screen.

The exchange rate is only one part of the transaction. Rate conditions, network selection, destination requirements, and applicable charges can all affect the result. Understanding these details before sending funds can help you avoid unpleasant surprises.

Imagine exchanging USDT for another currency. The displayed rate looks competitive, so you prepare to proceed. Then you discover the quote is an estimate, or the rate may change before the exchange is processed.

That does not automatically make the service unreliable. It means you need to understand the conditions behind the offer.

Before confirming, ask one straightforward question: How much should I expect to receive when the transaction is completed?

The answer is more useful than the headline rate alone. If the service doesn’t clearly explain how it calculates the final amount, take time to review its terms before proceeding.

Why the Best-Looking Rate May Not Be the Best Deal

Two exchange services can show similar rates but offer different conditions. One may use a floating rate that changes with the market, while another may offer a fixed rate for a specified period.

Consider two hypothetical offers. The first promises a slightly higher estimated return, but the amount can change before processing. The second displays a lower figure under clearly stated conditions. The first might still be attractive, but its initial advantage is less meaningful if the rate changes.

There is no universal winner. Compare the expected amount received, the conditions attached to the quote, and any applicable charges rather than choosing based on one number.

Find out whether the rate is fixed or floating. A fixed rate may apply only for a limited period and under specific conditions. A floating rate can change as the market moves. Knowing which applies helps you understand how reliable the displayed amount is.

USDT is available on multiple networks, and they are not automatically interchangeable. Check that the sending and receiving sides support the same intended network. An incompatible transfer can result in delays or lost funds.

Sending cryptocurrency to a wallet differs from receiving money through a bank or payment service. Traditional payment routes may have additional requirements, so confirm that your intended destination is supported before starting.

Some routes accept only transactions within specified limits. Check these restrictions beforehand, especially if you are exchanging a small balance. Do not assume every amount will qualify.

Review the transaction details to understand which charges apply and whether the displayed return is an estimate. If the information is unclear, do not assume that the quoted amount is what you will receive.

When considering Boomchange, focus on the particular exchange route rather than assuming one quote tells the whole story.

Visit the Boomchange website to check the available options. Before submitting a transaction, review the currencies, amount, destination details, and rate conditions shown for your chosen route.

Availability is important. A route offered for one currency or payment method does not necessarily mean every other combination is supported. Check the live interface to confirm that your intended transaction is available.

It is also worth asking whether you understand each step. Can you identify the amount being sent? Is the expected return visible? Are the applicable conditions clear? Knowing what to expect makes it easier to decide whether to proceed.

You do not need a complicated calculation to assess an exchange. A few checks can prevent common mistakes.

First, confirm the sending amount and the currency you expect to receive. Verify the destination details and, for cryptocurrency transfers, the selected network. Then review the quoted rate, any disclosed charges, and whether the amount is fixed or subject to change.

Consider your purpose, too. If you need a specific sum to cover a payment, an uncertain estimate may not be suitable. If you are transferring crypto between compatible wallets, network compatibility and transfer costs may matter most.

For an unfamiliar route, a smaller test transaction can help you understand the process, as long as it meets the service’s minimum requirements. It does not eliminate every risk, but it may be preferable to committing a larger amount immediately.

Crypto prices can move while you are comparing services. With a floating rate, the amount available when you begin may differ from the amount available when the exchange is processed.

Check the quote close to when you intend to transact, note any validity period, and review the details again before confirming. If the terms change significantly, reassess the transaction rather than proceeding simply because you have already prepared it.

A competitive quote can make an exchange worth considering, but it should never be the only factor in your decision.

The actual outcome depends on the rate conditions, asset, network, destination, and applicable charges. An attractive headline figure is less useful when important details remain unclear.

When evaluating Boomchange, check the available route, read the transaction conditions, and confirm the expected result before sending funds. Understanding the complete offer is a better basis for a decision than choosing whichever number looks best.

Why might the final amount differ from the quote?

Possible reasons include market movements, network costs, applicable fees, or other transaction conditions. The exact explanation depends on the route and the service’s terms.

Is the highest exchange rate always the best choice?

No. The final amount, rate conditions, and applicable charges matter just as much as the displayed rate.

Should I check the network before exchanging USDT?

Yes. Make sure the sending and receiving sides support the intended network and verify the destination details before transferring funds.

Does Boomchange support every payment route?

Do not assume that every route is available. Check the live interface to confirm support for your intended currencies and destination.

What should I review before confirming a transaction?

Check the amount being sent, expected return, rate conditions, applicable charges, destination details, and network where relevant. If anything is unclear, pause and review the terms.

Dogecoin has just formed a death cross on its daily chart for the first time since 2026. The 50-day simple moving average (SMA) has crossed below the 200-day SMA, completing a death cross on the daily chart. The last time Dogecoin saw a death cross signal on its daily chart was in November 2025, which preceded months of downward price action.

The development comes only about three weeks after Dogecoin recorded a golden cross on its chart. On Oct. 5, Dogecoin's shorter-term moving average, the 50 DMA, moved above the 200 DMA in a bullish golden crossover.

Krisspax, a Dogecoin community member, highlighted this development in an X post: "We have a death cross on the Dogecoin chart when the 50-day SMA crosses below the 200-day SMA. It's only been about 3 weeks since we had a golden cross, the shortest crossover I've seen for DOGE of this type, stressing the volatility of Dogecoin trading."

The golden cross and death cross signals on Dogecoin's daily chart are unusually close to each other. There is about a 3-week gap between them, indicating a sudden change in momentum.

A golden cross is generally interpreted as a sign of improving medium-term momentum, while a death cross suggests that the shorter-term trend has weakened relative to the longer-term trend.

Dogecoin's price surprisingly rose ahead of the death cross signal, rising for three consecutive days to reach a high of $0.081 on October 29 before momentum slipped.

DOGE sharply fell to a low of $0.074 on Thursday, extending the drop on Friday to a low of $0.072, last seen in August 2026, as the market reacted to the news of Binance's $6.3 billion heist, deemed the largest in crypto history.

#5350. Crypto and Midterm Election: 3 Risks From Trump’s $5,000 Stimulus to Iran

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Crypto is facing a major political test as Americans head to the polls on November 3, with the US midterm election potentially reshaping regulation, stimulus expectations, and investor risk appetite.

Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress, while Democrats are seeking to regain power in at least one chamber. The outcome could determine if President Donald Trump advances his economic agenda or faces a tougher legislative road ahead.

For crypto, the midterm election comes with three major risks: Trump’s proposed $5,000 stimulus dividend, the future of stalled crypto legislation, and escalating tensions with Iran.

The election itself may not immediately change Crypto’s fundamentals. However, it could shift expectations around liquidity, regulation, and the financial markets.

Trump has promised a $5,000 dividend payment to adult US citizens if Republicans retain control of both the House and Senate. The proposal would cover 240 million adults, potentially costing around $1.2 trillion, and Trump has also suggested that tariff revenue could help fund the payments.

Trump may have just sealed the deal on stage in Dallas.He's promising a $5,000 dividend to every American adult if Republicans win the midterms — only condition is the money has to be spent in the U.S.I've never seen anything like this. pic.twitter.com/ypJP2fYsLj

A Republican victory could then strengthen expectations for additional household spending and potentially inject fresh liquidity into financial markets. We, in the crypto market, have historical reasons to watch stimulus closely.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, US stimulus checks coincided with extraordinary monetary easing and a powerful crypto rally. A Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland study found that the 2020 payments increased Bitcoin buy volume by 3.8%, while the associated price effect was modest.

The 2020–2021 rally also benefited from low interest rates, institutional adoption, and abundant liquidity. Hence, a new stimulus program could encourage retail investors to allocate more money toward Bitcoin and other risk assets.

However, the proposed dividend is not approved, and higher inflation expectations or Treasury yields could offset some of the bullish impact. If Democrats win control of Congress, Trump’s proposal could face a much tougher path toward approval.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

The Midterm election could also determine whether lawmakers make progress on the most-awaited crypto regulation, the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act. It aims to establish clearer rules governing digital assets and the division of responsibilities between US regulators.

The bill remains stalled after failing to advance through a Senate procedural vote in September. A Republican victory could improve its chances, although bipartisan support would still be necessary to overcome legislative hurdles.

A Democratic victory, particularly if the party takes control of the House, could bring increased scrutiny of Trump’s crypto-related ventures and campaign connections. That could delay legislation as lawmakers focus on investigations and oversight.

Still, a Democratic win would not automatically mean tougher crypto regulation. Bipartisan support for clearer digital asset rules remains possible, although the final legislation could look different from the current proposal.

The Midterm election presents a mixed outlook for crypto. A Republican victory combined with stimulus optimism, progress on crypto legislation, and Iran de-escalation would create a potentially bullish environment.

A Democratic victory could introduce regulatory uncertainty, while renewed conflict in the Middle East could pressure crypto regardless of the midterm election result. For us, the key question is whether political optimism can outweigh geopolitical risk.

Trump’s stimulus promise may offer a powerful bullish narrative, but crypto’s next major move could ultimately depend on improving liquidity or another inflationary shock.

The biggest immediate threat to crypto is not the midterm election, and it may come from outside Washington. The US carried out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm islands near the Strait of Hormuz. This revived concerns about escalation, even as diplomatic contacts continued.

#5349. Not Just Ledger: Karpeles Warns of Tampered Trezor Devices

The ex-CEO of the now-defunct Mt. Gox, Mark Karpeles, has flagged the potential compromise of Trezor hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, indicating that the recent supply chain attack on Ledger devices is not an isolated case.

"Ledger n'est pas la seule. @Trezor devices sold by CryptoBilis were also implanted," Karpeles said in an Oct. 30 post on X.

In his post, Karpeles advised customers who bought Trezor devices from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards to immediately transfer their cryptocurrency to new wallets with new recovery phrases.

He also offered to manually review potentially compromised devices, saying that he would be willing to cover the shipping fees if customers wished to get their wallets checked.

Karpeles's alert follows Trezor's confirmation that its security team was made aware of a credible report of a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device.

As detailed in Trezor's Oct. 30 announcement, the device in question was acquired through the online marketplace Tokopedia in Indonesia in August 2026.

The report on the suspected device was received by Trezor on Oct. 28, and a video interview with the customer was conducted.

That said, Trezor said it hasn't checked the device in question in person to verify the report.

The report states that the suspected compromised device has an extra board between the main board and the screen.

The extra board has a cellular module and an antenna that can receive data from the device, such as the wallet's recovery phrase.

Afterwards, the data can be sent via a mobile network when the hardware wallet is plugged in.

This suspected modus operandi is similar to the highly advanced hardware implants previously found in Ledger devices sold by CryptoBilis.

In fact, Ledger's investigation into suspicious fund losses involving the reseller began on Oct. 9. Later, it was confirmed that some Ledger devices had been physically tampered with.

On the same day, Trezor decided to cut ties with CryptoBilis as an authorized reseller.

Four devices bought by CryptoBilis customers have been checked by Trezor, but no signs of tampering have been found so far.

According to Trezor, no CryptoBilis customers have reported losing funds in connection with the suspected Trezor implant.

Despite this, Trezor recommends that affected customers create a completely new wallet instead of just restoring their existing recovery phrases on other devices.

While mainland China maintains a strict ban on cryptocurrency transactions, the American platform Solana Foundation has made a major step in the region by signing a strategic agreement with a local licensed issuer in Hong Kong, Anchorpoint Financial Limited.

The partnership launches the HKDAP stablecoin for retail payments and tokenized assets — this is the project's first direct collaboration with a public blockchain foundation.

The issuer Anchorpoint is a consortium of Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong), telecom operator HKT and Animoca Brands, which received the FRS01 license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

Integration with Solana provides instant issuance and redemption of the asset, opening a legal banking gateway for retail and for trading real-world assets (RWA).

The deal rests on Hong Kong’s Stablecoins Ordinance, which took effect on August 1, 2025: any issuer of a fiat-referenced stablecoin must hold an HKMA license, fully back the token with high-quality liquid reserves and redeem it at par.

Since the Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the US dollar within a 7.75–7.85 band, HKDAP effectively becomes another dollar-linked instrument, but one issued in a separate jurisdiction outside direct US regulation.

Solana's infrastructure is ready for this: according to rwa.xyz data as of October 30, 2026, the total RWA volume on the platform stands at $18.89 billion, of which $14.13 billion (around 75%) is made up of stablecoins with a monthly transfer volume of $370.94 billion across 13.56 million addresses.

Consolidating its position, Solana Foundation is joining Hong Kong's government program OASES, opening a local office and rolling out the TAP tokenization program together with PwC.

This infrastructure creates a legal track for big capital. While mainland China tests the digital yuan exclusively within state-controlled pilot zones, Hong Kong provides clear rules of the game for private business.

As a result, Standard Chartered and its partners get a fully legitimate settlement instrument, and the international market gets direct access to Hong Kong dollar liquidity via the Solana blockchain.

#5347. Circle Begins CCTP V1 Wind-Down Amid Doc Mismatch

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

Most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It says: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026."

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the company wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible."

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations."

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1."

The main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

As of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle said "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

For Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

For everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

#5345. Ledger CTO Sounds Alarm Over New Cryptographic Threats to Bitcoin

Two new cryptographic breakthroughs raise concerns over the future of Bitcoin (BTC) and other cryptocurrencies, according to Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet.

According to Guillemet's Oct. 30 post on X, a recent study shows that it might be easier to break the mathematics behind elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC), which is how Bitcoin is secured.

“Thought it was a bad week for crypto? You may have missed the real news,” wrote Guillemet.

Elliptic-curve cryptography works by making it practically impossible to solve the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem.

So far, the best general method to solve it has been Pollard’s rho algorithm. Its computational cost increases exponentially with key size.

Now, the researchers have presented a subexponential algorithm that might in theory solve it more efficiently.

There is a big caveat. It relies on another claim by OpenAI researchers that requires further investigation.

The new algorithm doesn’t put current cryptographic schemes at risk, Guillemet insisted.

The best attacks for popular curves, like secp256k1 for Bitcoin, NIST P-256 and Ed25519, are still based on Pollard’s rho.

The new one would only be more efficient for hypothetical curves of very large sizes. For now, it’s just theoretical.

The second breakthrough is a big advance in the efficiency of quantum computing attacks on elliptic-curve cryptography.

Guillemet referenced a public research project, ECDSA.fail, aimed at improving the efficiency of quantum computing attacks against elliptic-curve digital signatures.

Researchers managed to reduce the estimated quantum circuit cost by about 70% relative to what Google previously reported, the Ledger executive explained.

Current estimates put the cost at about 0.91 billion in the logical-qubit-times-Toffoli-gates metric, down from 2.99 billion in Google’s figures.

What’s more important is that the French quantum computing company Alice & Bob has published a new paper estimating that it’s theoretically possible to break Bitcoin's secp256k1 cryptography using fewer than 30,000 physical cat qubits in about an hour.

The same paper estimates that factoring RSA-2048 would require 22,593 cat qubits and take about 3.14 days.

Such a quantum computer does not exist, so there is no immediate risk to Bitcoin, Guillemet noted.

However, these findings are a reminder of how the estimated resources needed to break common cryptographic schemes keep shrinking.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) is showing signs of weakness again, as bearish technical indicators suggest the cryptocurrency could face another sharp decline. Despite several recovery attempts in recent months, SHIB is still stuck below major resistance levels, and selling pressure continues to dominate its price structure.

Three indicators in particular point to more downside risks.

One concerning development is the increase in trading volume that comes with SHIB's recent price declines. The latest daily candlesticks show stronger selling activity as the token approaches the $0.00000460–$0.00000480 support region.

Rising volume during downward movements usually means stronger seller participation rather than temporary market weakness. Unless buyers absorb this pressure, SHIB could struggle to defend its current levels.

A clear breakdown below $0.00000460 could expose the cryptocurrency to its previous lows near $0.00000420, followed by the psychologically important $0.00000400 level.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) gives another warning. On the daily chart, the indicator has slipped toward the lower end of its neutral range, which reflects weakening momentum.

Although SHIB is approaching oversold territory, this does not necessarily mean a recovery is coming soon. During long downtrends, RSI can stay low for a long time while prices keep falling.

A sustained move below the 30 threshold would confirm stronger bearish momentum and increase the likelihood of another downward move.

SHIB's moving-average structure also remains unfavorable. The cryptocurrency trades below several important moving averages, including its longer-term trend indicator.

Shorter-term averages are turning downward, which raises the possibility of more bearish crossovers. Such developments would reinforce the existing downtrend and could discourage buyers from entering the market.

The $0.00000520–$0.00000560 region is now an important resistance zone that SHIB must reclaim to improve its technical outlook.

With selling volume increasing, RSI weakening, and moving averages staying in a bearish alignment, SHIB faces substantial downside risks.

The immediate downside targets are $0.00000460 and $0.00000420, with $0.00000400 emerging as a possible deeper support level.

Unless SHIB reclaims its overhead moving averages and attracts stronger buying volume, the path of least resistance appears to remain downward.

XRP's 15.7% drop in October has brought the token to the most unpredictable crossroads of the year. Historical data from thirteen years of observations promise the market harsh November volatility. However, behind the optimistic figures of past years lies a serious methodological flaw capable of disorienting investors amid the current pressure.

The main trap for the market is the asymmetry of returns. According to Cryptorank, XRP's average November gain is an impressive +80.2%, but this figure is completely distorted by two isolated anomalies: a surge of +531.9% in 2013 and a rally of +281.7% in 2024. The month's median, a negative -10%, reflects reality much more accurately.

Historically, in most cycles, XRP closed November in the red. The fourth quarter, which so far consists of October alone, is already down -16.3%, in line with the asset's seasonal tendency toward correction that the averaged statistics mask.

The median is not a perfect guide either: thirteen observations are a small sample, and the market structure has changed. Since spot XRP ETFs launched in the US in mid-November 2025, the token has had an institutional demand channel that did not exist in earlier cycles.

Mathematical pessimism is reinforced by the real balance of power on the market at the end of October. The XRP price has fallen below the key support line of $1.30 and is trading around $1.25–$1.26, marking a local downtrend.

All the upward momentum built on investors' expectations has faded, opening the way for profit-taking by short-term players. Notably, the October decline follows a 48% gain in the third quarter, XRP's best Q3 in four years, which suggests that at least part of the current pressure is profit-taking after the rally rather than seasonality alone.

The situation is aggravated by an inevitable influx of supply amid a liquidity shortage. On Sunday, November 1, a scheduled unlock of 1 billion XRP from Ripple's escrow wallets will take place.

It is worth noting, however, that the escrow unlock is a routine monthly event that has followed the same schedule since 2017, and Ripple typically returns 600–800 million XRP to new escrow contracts. The real net addition to circulating supply is therefore closer to 200–400 million XRP.

Even so, against the backdrop of thin liquidity, this volume is enough to put additional pressure on the price, as it will enter the market simultaneously with macroeconomic pressure and the aftermath of the recent wave of forced liquidations of long positions worth more than $1.29 billion, caused by a security incident at the Binance exchange.

At the same time, the wave of liquidations has partially cleared excess leverage from the market. If funding rates stay negative and open interest does not recover, the bearish scenario may be capped by a short squeeze, which would make a retest of $1.30–$1.32 more likely than the statistics suggest.

#5341. XRP Reserves on Binance Hit Lowest Level Since 2022

As the broader crypto market continues to face intense selling pressure due to the prolonged market volatility seen over the past weeks, XRP appears to be seeing rising demand instead.

While its price is also struggling amid the market downturn, onchain data from crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that more tokens are leaving major exchanges instead, which could be interpreted as intense buying.

The data shows that XRP reserves on the world's largest exchange by volume, Binance, have dropped to their lowest level since December 2022.

As of October 30, Binance has seen its XRP reserve fall to 2.47 billion XRP from the 2.69 billion XRP it recorded on October 28, marking a sharp decline in its holdings in just two days.

This signals rapid accumulation from traders as it marks a decrease of about 8.18% in the amount of XRP available for sale on Binance, with over  220 million XRP withdrawn in just a two-day period.

While decreases in exchange reserves simply mean a reduction in the amount of XRP readily available for trading, it potentially reduces immediate selling pressure if demand remains steady, thereby providing a bullish outlook for the token.

Further data shows that the decrease in the XRP exchange reserve on Binance has coincided with falling XRP balances on several other major crypto exchanges, including Bybit and Bithumb.

The data shows that reductions seen on these exchanges were smaller compared to Binance, as Bybit's XRP reserves dropped from 306 million to 286 million XRP during the same period.

Bithumb, on the other hand, also recorded a decrease of 10 million XRP, with its reserves falling from 1.847 billion to 1.837 billion XRP, down approximately 0.54% during the same days.

While this indicates a broader reduction in exchange-held supply and XRP has remained volatile despite the shrinking supply, it is important to note that lower balances do not always mean that investors are accumulating XRP, which could be the reason XRP has yet to react to the trend.

#5340. XRP Bucks Bearish Market Mood With Nearly 8,000 New Wallets in One Day — But There’s a Catch

Ripple-promoted XRP may be struggling to shake off bearish price pressure, but its network activity is telling a very different story. Nearly 8,000 new wallets were created in a single day, marking one of the XRP Ledger’s strongest growth spikes of 2026. While the surge appears to signal renewed interest in the XRP ecosystem, there may be more to the numbers than meets the eye — and the underlying reason could change how investors interpret this apparent adoption boom.

The XRP Ledger witnessed a notable surge in new wallet creation, with activity reaching one of its highest daily levels in recent months. Data from Santiment shows that 7,934 wallets were created on Sunday, November 1, making it the network’s sixth-strongest day for wallet growth in 2026. The spike is particularly striking because it occurred over the weekend, when blockchain activity typically tends to slow.

🚨 XRP Adoption Accelerates While Price Hovers Near $1.25🌱 XRP network growth is accelerating fast. November 1st saw 7,934 new wallets created, the 6th highest daily total of 2026, despite Sunday usually being one of crypto’s quieter days for network activity.📈 The surge… pic.twitter.com/CIeC7iWOW8

Santiment suggested that the surge may be partly linked to the recent Binance security incident, noting that the hack could have encouraged more users to move their assets away from exchanges and into self-custody by creating new wallets.

The October 29 attack reportedly stole $6.3 billion in assets, including 233 million XRP worth about $296 million. The FBI attributed the breach to North Korean hackers operating under the name TraderTraitor. However, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, has rejected the accusation, describing Washington’s findings as a “grave political provocation,” according to South Korean news agency Yonhap.

In the aftermath of the $6B hack, some XRP holders may have withdrawn their tokens from centralized exchanges and transferred them to newly created personal wallets, giving them direct control over their private keys. This could help explain the increase in new addresses, although wallet creation alone does not establish that new investors entered the XRP market.

Nevertheless, Santiment highlighted a potentially positive interpretation of the wallet surge. “Strong network growth while XRP trades near $1.25 suggests usage is improving even while price remains under pressure,” the analytics platform noted. This suggests that activity across the XRP Ledger may be strengthening even as the token continues to face bearish price pressure.

According to Santiment’s analysis, XRP’s immediate pivot point sits around $1.25, while a move above $1.30 could signal the first sign of strengthening bullish momentum. Reclaiming that level would suggest buyers are regaining control after the recent price weakness.

Santiment added that network activity could offer further confirmation. If new-wallet creation remains above roughly 4,000 per day while XRP climbs back above $1.30, the bullish outlook would become more convincing.

“If new-wallet growth stays above roughly 4K per day while XRP reclaims $1.30, the setup becomes more constructive,” the analytics firm stated.

However, the signal could weaken if XRP falls below $1.20 and daily wallet growth drops under 3,000. That combination would suggest both market momentum and network activity are losing steam.

XRP was trading at $1.27 at press time, up 1.9 percent for the day, according to CoinGecko.

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has revealed the unexpected story behind an iconic XRP-themed T-shirt he wore at the Swell event, explaining how a technical milestone on the XRP Ledger became associated with a memorable price moment.

Schwartz, one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), was spotted wearing a T-shirt that showed a 'speedometer'-like inscription that pointed to 100, sparking curiosity among members of the XRP community.

X user @unknowDLT had asked Schwartz about the origin of the T-shirt he wore in an image that accompanied his tweet. "At this point, could you clearly explain what the T-shirt you're wearing means?" he asked.

@unknowDLT It was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. When we commissioned it, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1. So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it.

Schwartz responded that the T-shirt was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. "When the T-shirt was commissioned, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1," Schwartz further explained.

The timing caused some members of the XRP community to assume the "100" on the shirt referred to XRP reaching a price of $1 rather than the network's transaction speed.

"So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it," Schwartz added.

In the X discussion, the Ripple CTO Emeritus did not share exact details on the time when the T-shirt was commissioned.

XRP also traded around 30 cents ($0.30) at several points in its price history, so it may be hard to know exactly when, in the context of the Ripple CTO Emeritus's post. A walk-through of the XRP Ledger throughput chronology may provide a hint.

When performance testing began in February 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained 80 transactions per second. Incremental improvements were made over time as opportunities were uncovered.

Between March and June 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained between 120 and 490 transactions per second. In October 2015, XRPL saw a major throughput boost to 525 transactions per second, and in the following year, this nearly doubled to 1,100 transactions per second.

In July 2017, XRP was demonstrated to sustain a throughput of 1,500 transactions per second, which remains so to this day.

Devcon attendees got an unexpected laugh when Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin appeared on stage wearing a green cloak and a smiling mask. The unusual cosplay stole the spotlight as Bitmine ETH accumulation continued, with the company adding another 8,573 Ethereum to its massive treasury.

Buterin’s costume looked more suited to a fantasy game than one of crypto’s biggest developer gatherings. The playful Vitalik appearance offered a lighter moment at Devcon 8 in Mumbai, where developers and researchers are discussing Ethereum’s future.

Meanwhile, Bitmine Immersion Technologies is pursuing a much more serious mission: accumulating enough ETH to control 5% of its total supply. The company’s latest disclosure showed holdings of 6,060,506 ETH as of November 1, worth $13.7 billion at its current price of $2,261. Devcon 8 runs from November 3 to November 6 in Mumbai, bringing Ethereum developers, researchers, and ecosystem participants together for four days of talks and workshops. But Buterin’s unusual outfit delivered an unexpected highlight during the event.

The Vitalik Devcon appearance showed the lighter side of Ethereum’s culture, even as the network faces serious questions about adoption, scaling, and ETH’s market performance.

@VitalikButerin just opened Devcon and set the tone for the week.A formally verified OS, open silicon, self-sovereign healthtech, free discourse, private communication, trustworthy AI — these are all part of Ethereum's mission. https://t.co/51UfMsxk5o pic.twitter.com/TynzSuzmhX

🧵1/BitMine provided its latest holdings update for November 2, 2026$14.5 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":– 6,060,506 ETH at $2,261per ETH (per @coinbase)– 216 Bitcoin (BTC)– $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast– $82 million stake in Eightco Holdings…

Bitmine has also staked 5.23 million ETH, representing 86% of its holdings. The company estimates that its current staking position could generate around $358 million in annualized rewards, potentially rising to $415 million if its entire ETH treasury were staked.

That creates a second part of its Ethereum thesis. Accumulating the asset while generating yield from the network.

Ethereum’s bullish outlook rests on more than Bitmine’s buying activity. Staking removes ETH from immediate trading circulation, while institutional treasury accumulation can add another source of demand. Bitmine’s holdings alone now represent nearly one in every 20 ETH in existence.

The company’s growing staking position also shows Ethereum’s proof-of-stake model, where holders can earn rewards by helping secure the network. Bitmine’s projected staking income gives it an incentive to maintain its ETH exposure rather than simply trade around short-term price moves.

Price forecasts remain ambitious. Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee has suggested Ethereum could revisit its previous all-time high near $4,954 before the end of 2026, with $6,000 also emerging as a potential year-end target.

There are risks to the bullish thesis. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded substantial outflows during October, while ETH’s price performance remained under pressure. Institutional accumulation has not yet translated into a decisive market reversal.

Still, Bitmine’s continued buying, its massive staked position, and Ethereum’s potential price recovery are keeping long-term bulls engaged.

Vitalik and his Devcon cosplay may have provided the conference’s funniest moment, but Bitmine’s growing treasury is the more serious signal. If institutional demand returns and ETH breaks through key resistance, $6,000 could move back into the conversation.

Crypto stocks edged higher before Tuesday’s open, November 3, even as Nvidia, Costco and Nike joined the companies blocking tokenized versions of their shares on OKXICE, taking the count to 50, and an AI chip sell-off sent Seoul’s Kospi down 3.6%.

The bounce is small, and it follows a bad month. Coinbase traded at $138.74 at 13:00 UTC, up 0.7% from Monday’s close of $137.83, its lowest finish since February 2024. Robinhood, Strategy and Circle rose between 0.5% and 1.1%, and Galaxy led with 2.8% after losing 8.8% on Monday.

The bigger story for the sector is the pushback against tokenization. Objectors to OKXICE, the 24/7 venue for tokenized US stocks that OKX is building with NYSE owner ICE, went from 16 to 50 in 11 days. Today is the deadline for companies notified on October 4, so the list could still grow, while Coinbase, Robinhood and the other crypto names on it have yet to say no.

Asia offered no lift. After a 1.1% drop in the Nasdaq on Monday, Samsung and SK hynix dragged the Kospi to 5,648.79, Shanghai slipped 0.8%, and Tokyo was shut for a holiday. Only Hong Kong closed higher, and Bitcoin held steady through the session at $77,326.

Investors are DUMPING US tech stocks at a rapid pace:The Nasdaq 100 index has dropped -6.1% over the last 3 trading sessions, its biggest 3-day decline since the April 2025 Liberation Day selloff. $QQQ This also marks the 3rd-largest 3-day decline since the 2022 bear market.… pic.twitter.com/jNvmex3HZj

So why are so many companies saying no to tokenization, and why are markets red from Seoul to New York?

Because they would carry the risk and see little of the benefit. OKXICE, the venue OKX is building with NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange, wants to offer round-the-clock trading of US stocks as tokens, paid for in stablecoins.

Under the SEC’s exemption, a company can keep its shares off such a venue if an outside firm does the tokenizing. It has 30 days from notice to object, and the objections have come fast:

The newest 12 are Nvidia, Costco, Micron, CrowdStrike, Corning, IREN, USA Rare Earth, Bloom Energy, Nike, Palo Alto Networks, Reddit and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. They join Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, which runs its own blockchain unit and says it still likes the technology.

The fight is over shareholder rights, especially votes. “Right now companies like Goldman and Microsoft see all of the risk and none of the upside,” Injective’s COO Mirza Uddin told CNBC.

OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo isn’t backing down. “We are at the very beginning of the rollout of fundamentally different market structure,” he said at the October 30 press conference.

Discover: JPMorgan and Coca-Cola Block Tokenized Stocks on OKXICE as Objectors Hit 33. Coinbase and Robinhood Stay Out of the List

Only the crypto names avoided objection to tokenisation, along with several major US stocks. Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, BitGo and Securitize remain outside the objection list, as do Apple, Amazon, Tesla, SpaceX and Netflix.

One crypto-born company did say no. IREN, the Bitcoin miner that now earns more from renting computers to AI firms than from mining, objected in the latest batch.

Silence isn’t a yes, though. Venues get up to five business days to publish objections, so companies that answered this week may not show up until next week’s notice, and staying off the list doesn’t guarantee a stock will trade at launch.

The AI trade is cracking again. Big Tech results last week showed Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft will keep spending heavily on data centres and chips, and investors want to see faster returns first.

Monday’s selling on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq fell 1.1%, hit Asia’s chipmakers on Tuesday:

Seoul’s slide is the one to watch. The Kospi closed at a record 9,114.55 on June 22 and is now 38% lower, with 17% of that lost since the end of September.

Oil added to the strain. Brent climbed 1.7% to $106.58 after reports of limited US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after it fell more than 7% on hopes of new talks.

Hong Kong’s crypto stocks split. Exchange operator OSL rose 0.4%, and Boyaa Interactive, which holds Bitcoin, fell 5.1%.

They have been sold off with tech, then sold again for crypto. Every big name is down at least 12% since the end of September, and the first trading day after the Binance hack was the worst of the run.

Coinbase’s daily chart shows how far the slide has gone. The stock is $34 under its 50-day average and more than $50 under its 200-day, and Monday’s close was the lowest since February 2024.

COIN 1D chart. Source: Yahoo Finance (Nasdaq).

The tokenization fight won’t move share prices on its own. For crypto stocks, today’s pre-market bounce still has to survive Wall Street’s open and a long night of election results.

"If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible," Mishaboar wrote.

If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible. Use a device and wallet you trust to create the new wallet. If your wallet supports an additional passphrase, use it (and remember to write it down in your offline backups). NEVER reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does NOT make your funds safe. An ELI5: I know this is obvious to many of you, but in my experience some people don't realize that hardware wallets don't actually "contain" their coins. Your coins "live" on the blockchain. Your wallet only holds the keys that allow you to access and spend them. If someone else has a copy of those keys, they can access your funds from anywhere in the world, from any device where those keys are imported. They don't need your physical little device or your phone to access it.

Users are warned never to reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does not make funds safe either.

Mishaboar highlighted a critical security principle that may not seem obvious to all users: hardware wallets do not actually "contain" coins—the coins "live" on the blockchain. The wallet only holds the keys that allow access to and spending of the coins. If someone obtains these keys, they can access the funds from anywhere in the world on any device where the keys are imported, without needing the physical device or the user's phone.

Mishaboar's warning follows a recent update from Trezor regarding CryptoBilis, in which the company disclosed that it had been alerted through responsible disclosure to a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device purchased from CryptoBilis in August 2026.

According to Trezor, the reported device has not yet been received for physical examination. However, the company said it considers the report credible enough to notify customers while its security team investigates. No CryptoBilis buyer has reported losing funds to the company so far.

In light of this, affected users are urged to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Those who have not yet set up their device should never do so using an existing wallet backup (recovery phrase), nor share this information with anyone.

#5332. Akash’s Solana Migration Clears November 2 Vote at 97%, With Four More On-Chain Decisions Ahead

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It shows how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:

It also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain."

A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis."

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

The portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks."

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence shows what that requirement means on-chain.

So Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

It's the 18th anniversary of the Bitcoin whitepaper. Today marks the historic date on which its pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto published the blueprint for the first digital cash.

On Oct. 31, 2008, a nine-page white paper called "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System" was published, laying out a radical vision for transferring value electronically without the need for conventional financial intermediaries.

Bitcoin supporters, exchanges, and the rest of the crypto community are filling social media platform X with celebratory wishes on the 18th anniversary of Bitcoin's unveiling to the world.

Bitcoin proponent and Strategy Chairman Michael Saylor wrote on X: "Happy Bitcoin white paper day. 18 years."

One of the most salient features of the whitepaper is the fixed supply of Bitcoin at 21 million coins. The pre-determined issuance structure is what makes Bitcoin different from traditional monetary systems, where central authorities can inflate the money supply.

Major U.S. crypto exchange Coinbase highlighted this fact in its X post: "21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day. https://t.co/JtKeHtCuSM

"Today marks 18 years since the release of the Bitcoin Whitepaper. A day that changed everything," Coinbase continued.

Stablecoin issuer Tether wrote: "On 31 October 2008, Satoshi published nine pages that explained Bitcoin to the world. Today we're explaining it to everyone else. Two pizzas, 10,000 BTC, 21 million coins, and one key you never share. Everything you need to know, in a comic. Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin whitepaper."

Crypto platform Uphold wrote: "Nine pages that challenged the entire legacy financial system. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

The Bitcoin whitepaper laid the groundwork for the network's launch in January 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto mined Bitcoin's genesis block and introduced the first units of the cryptocurrency.

When Bitcoin launched on January 3, 2009, it had no market value or official exchange price. Over the years, Bitcoin has evolved from a niche technological experiment into a globally recognized digital asset. Its emergence has influenced the development of thousands of cryptocurrencies, blockchain applications, and decentralized financial systems.

The cryptocurrency now trades at $77,310 and is worth $1.55 trillion, according to CoinMarketCap data.

#5329. Could You Handle Losing $741 Million? Crypto Community Revisits 8,999 BTC Mystery as Market Stays Muted

With the crypto market remaining undecided and major assets led by Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) recording only small price movements, the crypto community is revisiting stories of Bitcoin fortunes lost through irreversible mistakes.

Several X users raised these cases this week, including one of an early Bitcoin holder who reportedly lost access to thousands of coins now worth about $741 million.

Notably, while the coins remain visible on the blockchain, their owner, known as Stone Man, appears to have lost access to the wallet needed to recover them.

The incident dates back to August 10, 2010, when Stone Man described his predicament in a BitcoinTalk forum post titled “Lost large number of bitcoins.”

He explained that he had accumulated 9,000 BTC through an exchange and transferred the holdings to a Bitcoin client running on a Debian Linux live CD.

After backing up his wallet file to a flash drive, he attempted to send one Bitcoin to himself. However, he closed the Bitcoin program (client) before the transaction received confirmations, shut down the computer, and subsequently reloaded an older wallet backup.

His balance then showed only 1 BTC, alongside a transaction indicating that 8,900 BTC had been sent to an unfamiliar address.

“I do have the address that the 8,900 were supposedly sent to, but the old wallet file is gone for good,” he wrote.

The original BitcoinTalk post referred to 8,900 BTC, but the figure appears to have been a mistake. ZyCrypto confirmed that the associated Bitcoin address holds 8,999.00689948 BTC, according to blockchain records.

Another incident in May 2024 showed that not every major crypto loss ends the same way. An address-poisoning attack led to the theft of approximately $72 million in wrapped Bitcoin, prompting the victim to negotiate directly with the recipient.

“You’ve won, brother. You can keep 10% and return the 90%. We can act like nothing happened,” the victim wrote in an on-chain message.

The parties agreed that the recipient could retain 10% as a bounty in exchange for returning the remainder, and funds began moving back to the victim.

However, such recoveries depend on circumstances and, in some cases, the recipient’s cooperation. Blockchain transactions are generally difficult to reverse, while lost private keys can leave assets inaccessible indefinitely.

Moreover, the story echoes the case of James Howells, a British IT worker who said he accidentally discarded a hard drive containing the private keys to approximately 8,000 BTC in 2013. The drive reportedly ended up at a landfill in Newport, Wales.

As Bitcoin’s price climbed over the years, the lost coins’ potential value grew into the hundreds of millions of dollars. Howells pursued efforts to search the landfill, including proposals involving excavation and environmental safeguards, but Newport City Council opposed the plans. He abandoned the effort in 2025 after years of unsuccessful attempts to recover the hard drive.

Estimates from digital asset custody firm BitGo suggest that between 2.3 million and 4 million BTC may have been permanently lost, representing a significant share of Bitcoin’s 21 million maximum supply.

However, the exact figure remains uncertain because dormant wallets cannot automatically be classified as inaccessible, and some holders may still control their coins despite years of inactivity.

#5327. Zcash Upgrade Could Triple Transaction Speed as ZEC Faces Crypto Governance Turmoil

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Zcash is preparing to triple transaction speed as its NU7 network upgrade approaches November 5, but governance tensions and falling prices are testing investor confidence.

The Zcash upgrade will reduce target block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, making transaction confirmations significantly faster. The activation is planned for block height 3,543,405, according to the network’s deployment schedule.

Zcash Network Upgrade 7 mainnet activation height is being set for Block 3,543,405 (~November 5th 2026) pic.twitter.com/C4D5Dch61l

The technical changes arrive as Zcash faces a separate debate over its community-grants funding system. ZEC has also suffered recent price weakness, leaving traders weighing network improvements against growing uncertainty over its future direction.

The upcoming Zcash upgrade introduces several changes beyond faster block production. Under ZIP 218, the network will target a new block every 25 seconds, down from 75 seconds. That could reduce the waiting time for three transaction confirmations from nearly four minutes to around 75 seconds.

The upgrade also introduces limits on shielded transaction activity, designed to improve network efficiency and protect wallets against spam.

Meanwhile, ZIP 235 will remove 60% of transaction fees from circulation and place them into a reserve. The mechanism is intended to support future mining rewards as block subsidies decline.

Node operators must also upgrade their software to remain on the network’s consensus chain. at present, Zcash Foundation has released Zebra 7.0.0, which supports NU7 on mainnet and includes additional synchronization and security improvements.

The Zcash Upgrade comes as the project faces renewed debate over how its development ecosystem should be funded. Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe recently proposed ending the automatic allocation of 8% of newly issued ZEC to the Zcash Community Grants program.

Bowe said that the program already holds approximately $125 million after existing commitments, enough to fund years of development without continuing automatic inflows.

His proposal would redirect the allocation toward a reserve supporting future mining rewards. The committee would retain its existing funds and continue distributing grants.

The proposal does not directly cite that controversy, instead focusing on the size of the grants treasury and long-term funding sustainability.

ZEC has also faced selling pressure ahead of the upgrade. Recent market coverage placed the token near $1,135 after an approximately 11% decline, highlighting the disconnect between improving network fundamentals and short-term price performance.
