#5325. Binance to Resume XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum and Other Crypto Withdrawals

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance will allow withdrawals for major cryptocurrencies such as XRP, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL), among others, after suspending withdrawals because of a massive security breach involving $6.3 billion.

Binance announced on Nov. 1 that the exchange would begin resuming withdrawal services between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC.

Binance emphasized that the withdrawal resumption process will be carried out progressively as the exchange conducts security and infrastructure readiness checks.

"We aim to restore withdrawals progressively as we complete security and readiness checks," said Binance.

Binance continued to offer deposit services during the security breach.

The first phase of withdrawal resumption will include a total of 15 blockchain networks.

This list includes popular networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Ledger, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, and Dogecoin.

Other cryptocurrencies that will be available for withdrawals include Zcash (ZEC), Avalanche (AVAX), Sui (SUI), Polygon (POL) and Arbitrum (ARB).

Withdrawals of major stablecoins such as Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) will also be enabled on multiple networks.

The exchange noted that it selected the assets based on user withdrawal demand over the past week.

The exchange also warned that not all listed cryptocurrencies and networks may be enabled at the same time.

The withdrawal resumption comes only days after Binance suffered a massive security breach.

The breach led to the theft of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the exchange's hot wallets.

The exchange temporarily paused withdrawals in order to contain the damage, conduct an investigation into the security breach and avoid additional losses.

Binance has now disclosed that it has recovered around 95% of affected assets.

This is up from 90% when Binance last provided an update on the recovery process.

The exchange said that it has fully backed the balances of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, BNB, USDT, USDC, Zcash, USD1, and Ripple USD (RLUSD).

The remaining 5% includes cryptocurrencies that are less liquid and harder to buy in large amounts.

#5323. Do Not Use Your iPhone as Hardware Wallet, OneKey Founder

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Using an old iPhone as a crypto cold wallet may be less safe than it looks, OneKey founder Yishi Wang has warned. The practice is popular with self-custody fans: wipe a spare phone, take it offline, and keep your wallet recovery information on it.

Wang's worry is that an offline phone can still be attacked by someone who has it in their hands. He has pointed to flaws in several generations of iPhone. These include the publicly documented checkm8 issue on older models and, more recently reported, low-level weaknesses in certain later devices. They sit in the early stages of the boot process. A malicious app isn't involved.

An iOS update may not fix a weakness built into immutable boot code. Switching off Wi-Fi and cellular does nothing about someone who gets physical access to the phone. A vulnerability still doesn't automatically mean an attacker can recover a seed phrase, though. Device encryption, passcode strength and secure key handling remain real barriers.

Wang advises against trusting iPhone 11-generation and older devices with recovery phrases. If you think a phrase may have been exposed, create a completely new one using a trusted setup and move your funds to that wallet. Generating another address from the same seed won't help, because the underlying exposure stays.

He also stresses updated operating systems, long alphanumeric passcodes and careful control of USB connections. Earlier, he suggested that even newer iPhones shouldn't be treated as equivalent to purpose-built signing devices when the holdings are substantial and long-term.

Dedicated hardware wallets are built to isolate signing keys and let you check transaction details on the device itself. They carry risk too. Counterfeit hardware, compromised distribution channels and sloppy recovery-phrase handling can all undermine their security.

The argument is about threat models, not brand loyalty. An offline phone cuts remote exposure, but that doesn't turn it into a secure hardware wallet.

#5322. Binance’s $6.3B Hack Fix Is Coming Tomorrow: Why the ZK Math Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot shows its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

A reported $1.1 billion in NEAR Protocol derivatives open interest has put the spotlight on speculative positioning in the token. The exact figure and its timing need confirmation at the exchange level. The general point holds either way: leveraged trading magnifies both optimism and downside when interest in an asset picks up.

Open interest is the notional value of futures and perpetual futures contracts that are still open. Daily trading volume is something else, a count of transactions over a period. Rising open interest means more positions are staying active. It doesn't say whether traders as a group expect prices to rise or fall, since every contract has exposure on both sides.

NEAR's derivatives participation has been swining before. In October open interest climbed above $1 billion and approached $1.9 billion during a strong price rally, then a pullback.

To read a fresh increase, analysts usually compare open interest with spot price, funding rates, trading volume and liquidation data. When price and open interest rise together, the market often reads that as growing risk appetite. If prices fall while open interest stays high, crowded leveraged positions become vulnerable to forced exits.

Funding rates are just another source of data. Sustained positive funding can suggest stronger demand for leveraged longs, and negative funding a preference for shorts. Neither is conclusive alone, and differences between exchanges can muddy comparisons.

NEAR's longer-term prospects depend on more than derivatives. Transaction costs, ecosystem integrations and adoption of cross-chain infrastructure such as NEAR Intents are more longer-term drivers. Speculative positioning can move the price fast, but it is no substitute for durable demand for blockchain services.

New leveraged positions must be backed by spot-market buying and healthy liquidity in order to have relevance. A large open-interest figure shows attention, nothing more. It isn't a forecast. Check it across data providers and manage risk carefully.

#5319. Ripple Urges SEC to End “Case-by-Case” Crypto Enforcement, Citing $150M XRP Legal Fight

Ripple is calling on the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to ditch its “case-by-case” approach to crypto enforcement and establish clear rules for the industry, warning that regulatory uncertainty is driving innovation offshore and costing companies millions in legal battles.

Ripple Chief Legal Officer Stuart Alderoty announced Wednesday that the company had submitted a comment letter supporting the SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework.

The filing argues that the agency can establish clearer requirements under existing securities laws without waiting for Congress to pass comprehensive crypto legislation.

“Years of ‘case by case, coin by coin’ enforcement has pushed innovation offshore,” Alderoty wrote on X. “We need holistic rules for digital assets.”

Ripple also argues that regulators should distinguish between a digital asset and the investment contract associated with its sale.

“The investment contract is the security, not the token,” Alderoty stated, adding that the focus should be on what an issuer promised investors and when those obligations end, rather than relying on a subjective decentralization test.

Notably, Ripple’s position reflects its prolonged legal dispute with the SEC, which began in December 2020 when the regulator accused the company of conducting an unregistered securities offering through XRP sales.

In July 2023, a federal court ruled that Ripple’s programmatic XRP sales to retail buyers on exchanges did not constitute investment contracts under the circumstances examined. However, the court found that certain institutional sales violated securities registration requirements.

The case continued through subsequent proceedings before Ripple and the SEC reached a settlement in 2025, resolving the long-running dispute.

Ripple has since used the litigation to illustrate the financial consequences of regulatory uncertainty. In its latest submission, the company said its legal expenses exceeded $150 million.

“No company should have to do that to learn what the law requires,” Alderoty wrote.

CEO Brad Garlinghouse has similarly argued that the XRP case demonstrates why the industry needs predictable regulations.

Following the Senate’s September setback on the CLARITY Act, he said Ripple had obtained legal certainty for XRP through the court process, even as the broader industry continues to seek clearer rules.

At an October 15 appearance on “The Starting Block” podcast, Garlinghouse also argued that regulatory progress could continue through agency action despite the legislative impasse.

“You can’t put the genie back in the bottle,” he said, referring to the momentum behind crypto regulation and adoption.

That said, Ripple’s filing comes as Congress struggles to advance legislation defining the SEC’s and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s (CFTC) regulatory responsibilities.

The CLARITY Act failed a Senate procedural vote on September 15, receiving 49 votes in favor and 50 against. The motion needed 60 votes to advance to floor debate.

Disagreements over ethics provisions involving President Donald Trump and his family’s cryptocurrency interests contributed to the impasse. Although the bill has not been permanently abandoned, its immediate legislative prospects have weakened.

The SEC, meanwhile, is pursuing its own regulatory framework. Proposed in August, Regulation Crypto Assets would create tailored exemptions for certain crypto-related investment contracts and a conditional safe harbor for assets that meet specified requirements.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins has presented the proposal as part of the agency’s effort to provide clearer pathways for crypto businesses while maintaining investor protections.

The cryptocurrency market is breaking the classical rules of financial economics. The industry has faced the biggest challenge in its history: the FBI confirmed that North Korean hackers attacked Binance's infrastructure and withdrew $6.3 billion.

However, instead of a protracted capitulation, this news triggered a paradoxical reaction: prices held, creating a strong bullish precedent.

Against this backdrop, well-known crypto analyst DonAlt, who accurately predicted the historic 700% XRP rally back in 2024, directly cites the Binance hack as the reason for his ultra-bullish sentiment. In his opinion, in the current situation it is "hard to be a bear" precisely because of how the market reacted to the catastrophe.

The situation was promptly stabilized by the actions of the platform itself, which acted proactively and covered 90% of users' lost funds from its own reserves, and by the Treasury Department. As a result, Bitcoin ignored attempts at mass sell-offs and held around $77,935, while XRP settled at $1.2498.

The main indicator for the analyst was the complete absence of panic follow-through selling after the shocking news. DonAlt draws a direct analogy with the events of November 2022, when the industry was going through the collapse of the FTX exchange:

"Last time the market didn't properly sell off after a huge event like this was the FTX collapse. When I saw the lack of follow through then I got giga bullish. And we subsequently went from 16k to 100k. Hard to be bearish here after having been given the same setup yet again"

The expert emphasizes that there are no 100% guarantees in financial markets and classifies the current situation as a game of mathematical probabilities. According to him, when the market prices in colossal negativity but refuses to go down, the odds in the long run are always on the side of buyers.

Still, DonAlt’s argument rests on a single precedent. The FTX analogy worked once, but one case is not a pattern, and the two events differ in important ways. FTX wiped out customer funds for good, while in the Binance case most losses were covered within days.

A market that does not fall on a compensated hack is responding rationally, not necessarily showing hidden strength.

The real test will come in the next few weeks: if prices hold once the news is fully priced in and attention shifts to the stolen funds moving through mixers, the bullish case gets much stronger. If they don’t, the lack of follow-through may turn out to have been only a delay.

#5317. Why Didn't Bitcoin Drop More? Binance's CZ Credits FBI

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) credited the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other US law enforcement agencies with helping prevent a larger drop in the Bitcoin (BTC) price after the massive $6.3 billion security breach at the Binance cryptocurrency exchange.

Binance founder CZ commended the timely actions of the FBI, US Secret Service (USSS), and Internal Revenue Service (IRS) amid the massive security breach.

According to CZ's Nov. 1 post on X, US law enforcement agencies (FBI, USSS, IRS and more) helped "a lot" during the incident.

For instance, they helped with tracking and freezing funds.

According to the Binance co-founder, they were able to prevent an even sharper fall in the Bitcoin price.

"Not enough to express our appreciation in a tweet. There are probably a lot of crypto bros not realizing that a lot of 'why bitcoin didn't drop even more?' credits go to them," CZ stated.

This comes after the FBI officially identified North Korean hackers as being behind the record-breaking Binance hack.

According to the FBI's Oct. 31 announcement, North Korea stole more than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the Binance crypto exchange on or about Oct. 29.

More specifically, the FBI identified the North Korean cybercrime group TraderTraitor as being behind the massive cryptocurrency theft.

It's a known North Korean hacker group that has stolen large amounts of cryptocurrencies before.

The FBI noted that investigators, together with the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, have tracked how the hackers were exchanging stolen cryptocurrencies mainly for Ethereum (ETH).

The FBI warned that these assets could be further laundered using decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols and instant cryptocurrency swap services.

The US authorities have called on cryptocurrency businesses and infrastructure providers to block transactions related to the cryptocurrency addresses used by the hackers to stop them from laundering these assets.

Specifically, the US authorities urged THORNode operators, remote procedure call (RPC) node operators, instant exchanges, blockchain analytics companies, DeFi platforms, etc., to block such transactions.

Apart from that, the FBI provided a list of the cryptocurrency addresses used by the hackers to allow other members of the cryptocurrency industry to detect and block suspicious transactions.

The Binance security breach sent shock waves throughout the cryptocurrency market.

Bitcoin tumbled below $77,000 after the market reacted to the unprecedented crypto theft.

BTC dropped to around $76,000 at one point, registering its lowest price in several weeks.

Meanwhile, other major cryptocurrencies like Ethereum, XRP, Solana (SOL), and BNB nosedived as the market reacted to the breach.

Fortunately, Bitcoin eventually found stability and was trading around $78,000 during the early Nov. 1 trading session.

That would put Bitcoin Layer 2 projects in a different conversation, not simply as faster payment rails for retail users, but as potential infrastructure for tokenized assets and cross-network settlement.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. A headline claiming that 1.8 billion XRP moved across the XRP Ledger within 24 hours has revived discussion of a network recovery. The figure hasn't been independently verified for a dated 24-hour period, so treat it as a reported claim, not confirmed evidence of a new trend.

The XRP Ledger handles payments, decentralized exchange transactions and tokenized assets. Payment volumes reflects the network activity, but the number needs context. Large transfers can be exchange custody movements, internal treasury operations or transfers between wallets controlled by the same entity.

None of that necessarily signals fresh investor demand or new capital entering the market.

Recent verified reporting shows why the distinction matters. One October snapshot had daily payment volume jumping to about 137.7 million XRP, still below its 30-day average of roughly 496 million.

Another October reading, around 363.3 million XRP, came with the same caution: a one-day rise did not establish a sustained recovery.

A reading near 1.8 billion XRP usually comes at the end of the week where most of the network activity occurs. The most likely outcome is always the same: high activity by Thursday and Friday and a tubmling on the weekend, with a recovery starting on Monday.

Other indicators help separate real adoption from a passing spike: active addresses, successful payment counts, decentralized-exchange trading, liquidity and how transaction sizes are distributed. Even high transaction counts can mislead when automated activity dominates, as recent investigations into small-value stablecoin payments on XRPL showed.

Network usage and XRP's market price are only indirectly related. More settlement activity doesn't guarantee higher token prices, and speculative buying can lift prices with no matching improvement in usage. Broader market conditions and exchange liquidity matter too.

A verified natural burst of XRP movement could mean renewed engagement with the network. A more convincing signal would be several consecutive days of stronger, widely distributed activity, backed by improving liquidity and sustained user demand, which rarely happens.

In late October 2026, Zcash (ZEC) reached a key milestone: the coin's price consolidated around $1,280, and its market capitalization hit $21.8 billion. However, the rapid rally was overshadowed by a sharp split within the community.

The trigger of the crisis was not a technical problem but a revolt of large investors over the targeted spending of capital.

Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the organization that distributes part of the miners' block reward, launched the Zcash Adoption Pool program. The fund directed grants toward the integration of vulnerable groups like refugees without access to banks.

The decision sparked protest from major players, since ZCG's charter allows it to distribute multimillion-dollar budgets bypassing the coinholder vote. The "whale" revolt moved into the practical realm: a major holder under the pseudonym "big z" publicly announced a full sell-off of his ZEC holdings.

According to him, the fund should finance cryptography, not political manifestos.

The local conflict quickly grew into a debate about the nature of decentralized money, which industry heavyweights joined. Developer Sean Bowe published a manifesto on the future of ZCG, in which he called for revising the fund's financing due to the anomalous surge in the ZEC price.

The initiative was unexpectedly supported by legendary investor Naval Ravikant, who laconically snapped that a $50 million cap is more than enough for community grants.

Meanwhile, the fund's activists continue to insist that private money is a "humanitarian imperative" and a public good.

However, Gemini exchange co-founder Tyler Winklevoss harshly challenged this thesis: a commercial network with transaction fees cannot be a public good. Winklevoss compared ZCG's actions to "taxation without representation" and called for leaving the development of Zcash to the free market.

The pressure on the price from the whales' coin sell-off coincided with the launch of direct ZEC deposits on the decentralized Rujira Network on October 29.

After failing to break above $1,390, the price settled in the $1,220–1,245 $range, still well below the all-time high of $1,698 set in late September. The fundamental dispute over who should control Zcash's millions remains open.

#5309. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

Frustration is growing among parts of the XRP community, with one investor accusing Ripple of prioritizing its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin ambitions and leaving longtime XRP holders behind. In an emotional appeal, the investor called on the company’s leadership to recognize the community’s years of loyalty and take action to help unlock XRP’s long-anticipated $20 valuation. The message has reignited debate over whether Ripple’s expanding business strategy will ultimately translate into meaningful gains for XRP holders.

In a November 1 post on X directed at Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse and Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz, XRP investor Fabrizio Scudu criticized the company for allegedly prioritizing its Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin and its broader corporate expansion at the expense of XRP holders. Specifically, he accused Ripple of redirecting XRP’s economic and technological potential toward the stablecoin and other enterprise initiatives, arguing that the company was securing its own future while leaving longtime investors behind.

Scudu said the community had stood by Ripple through nearly a decade of negative sentiment, financial uncertainty, and its prolonged legal wrangle. In his view, investors did more than simply purchase a cryptocurrency; they supported the company through a difficult period, with some committing personal savings and staying loyal to the XRP ecosystem.

To Brad Garlinghouse and David Schwartz: A message for your souls by the fireside.When you sit by the fireside of your homes in the evening, enveloped in the peace and warmth of your families, I look upon you and ask you to look into your souls. That sense of peace, that right to…

Scudu accused Ripple’s leadership of securing the company’s future while leaving longtime XRP holders uncertain about their own financial prospects. He urged the executives to acknowledge the community’s loyalty and sacrifices, arguing that investors deserve to benefit from the ecosystem they helped support through years of challenges.

He also called on Ripple to take meaningful action to help XRP reach what he considers its fair market value of $15 to $20 or higher. In his closing appeal, Scudu framed the issue as one of loyalty and accountability, warning that the community’s contributions should not be forgotten as Ripple continues to expand its business operations. “History is watching you, and so is God,” he concluded.

Meanwhile, as criticism over Ripple’s growing RLUSD business continues to surface, CEO Garlinghouse has pushed back against suggestions that the stablecoin is taking priority over XRP. He recently emphasized during the Swell 2026 conference in New York that Ripple remains committed to its native ecosystem token, declaring, “We will never give up on XRP.”

Garlinghouse also described XRP and RLUSD as “very complementary,” arguing that the two assets serve different but interconnected purposes within Ripple’s broader payments strategy. While RLUSD offers the price stability needed for payments and financial transactions, XRP can provide liquidity and facilitate value transfers across the XRP Ledger.

Garlinghouse further reassured the XRP community that Ripple’s business decisions would not come at the expense of XRP. He stressed that the company “will never do something we think is bad for the XRP ecosystem,” reinforcing his position that RLUSD’s growth is not intended to undermine XRP.

Ultimately, the debate goes beyond Ripple’s growing business footprint. What matters to XRP holders like Scudu is whether that expansion will create meaningful demand for the token itself. More partnerships, payment channels, and RLUSD adoption may strengthen Ripple’s ecosystem, but none of these developments guarantees that XRP will capture enough value to reach the investor’s $20 ambition.

#5307. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5305. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

#5303. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

#5301. Yield-Bearing eZAR Blurs the Line Between Stablecoin and Investment Product

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

eZAR opened its rand-pegged token to the public on November 2 with R303 million in circulation. Its reserve yield is the feature that puts the stablecoin label to the test.

Most stablecoin launches promise a token that never moves. eZAR's disclosures say its holders can make money or lose it. The rand-pegged token went live to the public on November 2, and its fine print reads more like an investment product than a payments coin.

According to launch reports, eZAR is now open to the public and to new institutional partners after almost a year of pilot operations. The company says R303 million worth of tokens had been issued and were in circulation as of October 30.

The project is a partnership between eZAR Ltd, asset manager Ninety One and AVBOB Financial Services, with AVBOB acting as lead institution and liquidity partner. CEO Sean Emery said the team put "getting it right" ahead of "getting it big" during the pilot. The message now is that eZAR is ready to scale.

The model also departs from the typical single-issuer coin. Neobanks, retailers, insurers and payment firms can plug the token into their own branded wallets and share in the economics. Transfers between participating wallets settle within seconds at any hour and, according to the company, cost nothing.

The reserves backing eZAR are invested through a money market strategy run by Ninety One, mainly in the Ninety One Money Market Fund. Returns are distributed daily to partners after partnership fees, and each partner then decides on what terms its own customers receive a share.

Ninety One's head of digital assets, Adam Duxbury, described it as new rails under an old discipline. His firm has run money market strategies for 25 years, he said, and South Africa should build its own digital rand rather than import a dollar coin.

The framing is clever, since it presents the yield as a feature of "digital cash that can grow." Yet that same feature makes the classification question hard to avoid.

The risk language is the most revealing part of the launch. eZAR describes itself as a crypto asset issued by the eZAR En Commandite Partnership. It states that the token is not legal tender, not a bank deposit and not a banking product, and that it carries no guarantee.

The details that follow set it further apart. The R1 redemption value depends on available liquidity. Money market returns can be positive or negative, so capital is at risk. Holders also own no units in the underlying fund and have no direct claim on it.

"Capital at risk" rarely appears in stablecoin terms. A payments token is meant to hold its value and let users redeem at par, yet eZAR's own documents hedge on both counts. Back in March, a market survey from Blockhouse had already noted that eZAR doesn't qualify as a stablecoin under most regulations. The live launch now tests that observation against a real product.

In the major rulebooks, the yield is the sticking point. The US GENIUS Act bars permitted payment stablecoin issuers from paying holders any form of interest or yield solely for holding, using or retaining the token. The EU's MiCA framework takes a similar line on interest. The logic is that a payment token paying a return starts to function like an unregulated deposit.

The OCC issued its final GENIUS Act rules on October 21, and they confirmed that ban for covered issuers. The contested ground lies elsewhere, in who sits between the issuer and the holder. Earlier OCC proposals set a rebuttable presumption against yield arrangements run through affiliates and related third parties, whereas the statute itself names only issuers.

eZAR's design lands squarely in that gray zone. Returns flow to partners, and the partners decide how customers share in them. Whether that amounts to an issuer paying yield or a partner passing on profit is precisely the kind of question US regulators are now wrestling with, and it would be a difficult one to argue before the OCC.

eZAR doesn't operate under the US or EU regimes, so none of those rules apply to it directly. eZAR Ltd is described as an authorised financial services provider responsible for the main technology and services behind the partnership. That technology also draws on the South African Reserve Bank's Project Khokha 2, where eZAR's parent company, Block Markets Africa, was a technical contributor.

This background signals a serious, institution-backed build rather than a speculative launch. Even so, the rand stablecoin field is getting crowded. ZARU launched earlier this year as an institutional-grade rand coin, and a pattern is emerging of different models competing for the same local payments niche.

The bigger question is whether South Africa will define stablecoins narrowly, as the US and EU do, or leave room for hybrid products like this one. Because the network is permissioned, the reported circulation figure also rests on company disclosure rather than a public ledger, which makes the regulatory and disclosure framework matter even more.

For everyday users, the appeal is easy to see. A rand token that moves in seconds, costs nothing to send and might earn a daily return makes an attractive pitch. For partners, shared infrastructure with a revenue share offers a way into digital payments without building a coin from scratch.

The trade-off sits in the disclaimers. A holder who treats eZAR like a bank balance could be caught off guard by liquidity-dependent redemption, or by a money market return that dips below zero. That gap between how the product feels and how it is legally defined is where regulators tend to step in.

eZAR is best understood as a hybrid: a payments token with an investment return attached. It may well succeed on those terms. Still, as more jurisdictions tighten the stablecoin definition around no-yield, par-redemption tokens, products like this will increasingly be judged on what they are rather than what they are called. How South African regulators treat eZAR in the coming months will show which way that debate is heading.

The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

The engines surface those who have invested in AI visibility and optimized for how these models index and cite content. We ran the same buyer-intent queries across all three platforms in October 2026 to see who actually appears — and where.

We submitted five main queries to ChatGPT, Perplexity (standard and Deep Research), and Claude with web search enabled in October 2026. Queries covered three buyer intents: best crypto marketing agency, best blockchain marketing agency, and best crypto marketing agency for token launch. Agency name, position, and source URLs were recorded for all responses.

Positions below reflect the best crypto marketing agency query. Coverage Score = total appearances across all three platforms and all three query types (max: 9). Agency entries are ordered by that score.

ICODA is the top result on both Claude and ChatGPT for “best crypto marketing agency” — the only agency to hold both platforms simultaneously on that query.

What the engines say: Claude: #1 for crypto marketing and token launch, citing AI search visibility as a “2026 differentiator” (source: marketerhire). ChatGPT: #1 for both crypto and blockchain queries, tagged “best for integrated growth.” Perplexity standard: absent from the crypto shortlist, but #1 for token launch.

Where it wins: Quick-answer queries on Claude and ChatGPT. Both engines explicitly name AI search visibility as a differentiator — the only agency in this audit cited for it.

Notable strength: Full-cycle coverage — SEO, PR, KOLs, paid, community — with stated focus on each type and stage of crypto project.

Watch-out: ICODA’s own content is cited by Perplexity Deep Research to rank a competitor (MarketAcross), an unflagged self-citation loop.

MarketAcross is the most consistently cited PR-specialist — present on Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity across crypto and blockchain queries.

What the engines say: ChatGPT: #3 for both crypto and blockchain queries. Claude: #6 for crypto — “best for media authority and thought leadership.” Perplexity: present in both standard and Deep Research, ranking #4 in the blockchain Deep Research final table (sources: coincodex, icoda).

Where it wins: Institutional PR positioning. All three engines describe it in near-identical terms: media relations, thought leadership, credibility-building.

Notable strength: Verified client work with Polygon and Splinterlands (source: coincodex).

Watch-out: Perplexity Deep Research cited ICODA’s own agency comparison page to position MarketAcross as an “institutional PR leader.” The citation reads as independent; the source is commercially motivated.

Every token launch query on Claude and Perplexity returns Lunar Strategy in the top three.

What the engines say: Claude: #2 for blockchain marketing (“best for token launches, DeFi and NFT”) and #3 for token launch. ChatGPT: #3 for token launch, citing its TGE Accelerator. Perplexity standard: #3 for token launch (sources: Lunar Strategy + one additional). Absent from all standard crypto marketing shortlists on Perplexity.

Where it wins: Token launch and pre-TGE context — a rare cross-engine agreement on positioning.

Notable strength: Dedicated TGE Accelerator product; described as combining marketing with tokenomics consulting, differentiating it from PR-heavy agencies (source: marketerhire).

Watch-out: Query-type dependent visibility. Lunar Strategy does not surface on Perplexity’s standard crypto marketing shortlist.

NinjaPromo appears consistently on Claude and ChatGPT but is entirely absent from Perplexity across all query types tested.

What the engines say: Claude: #3 for both crypto and blockchain marketing, positioned for “performance and execution speed” (source: cbinsights). ChatGPT: #4 for crypto — “a broad digital marketing partner combining creative, social, paid campaigns, and branding.” Zero Perplexity appearances.

Where it wins: Claude positions NinjaPromo most strongly. GameFi and fintech are cited as strong-fit verticals by both engines.

Notable strength: Positioned as a full-stack outsourced marketing department — suited to teams that need multi-channel output without building in-house.

Watch-out: Buyers using Perplexity as their primary AI research tool will not encounter NinjaPromo on any query tested.

theKOLLAB surfaces in KOL-heavy contexts — not in general crypto marketing queries on all platforms.

What the engines say: Perplexity: #2 on the crypto shortlist — ahead of MarketAcross — citing Trust Wallet, Aptos Labs, and Tron as clients and 50M+ reported reach (source: coinranking). Claude: #7 for crypto. Absent from ChatGPT on all queries tested.

Where it wins: Perplexity’s crypto shortlist specifically, for KOL-driven token launches.

Notable strength: 250+ vetted crypto creators including Altcoin Daily and Crypto Lark. Claude cites a 1,230% token price increase for Orange Crypto at launch (source: dailycoin).

Watch-out: That 1,230% figure traces to dailycoin, not independent verification. All performance metrics are self-reported.

The agencies in this audit appear in AI search results because they have working AI visibility methodology — not by accident. If AI search visibility is a priority for your project, the practical starting point is agencies that already demonstrate it for themselves: they have the expertise and a proven process.

One caveat applies across the board: AI engines can surface inaccuracies, outdated information, and self-cited sources as independent ones. Before shortlisting any agency from an AI-generated result, verify their cases and results manually.

No single agency dominates all three platforms in this audit. In the crypto marketing agency 2026 results, ICODA leads standard results on Claude and ChatGPT — the two engines that drive the majority of quick buyer research. Perplexity runs its own shortlist. The same agency can rank #1 on two platforms and be absent from the third. AI search visibility is a real asset — and an engine-specific one.

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is set for a significant week ahead as its long-awaited cleanup upgrade heads for mainnet activation this week, bringing a wide-ranging collection of fixes and improvements to the blockchain.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the hackers behind the record $6.3 billion theft spent months working their way into the exchange, rejecting claims that one compromised laptop was to blame. Speaking to CNBC, Teng said the attack began in June, when a wallet DevOps engineer installed a tampered version of Homebrew while searching online for a popular AI coding tool. Binance spotted the activity and replaced the device, but the engineer’s team had already been exposed. In September, the attackers posed as recruiters and gave another engineer a coding test containing hidden malware. They then moved through Binance’s internal AI tools to reach the system that approves wallet transactions. Teng said 98% of the $6.34 billion has been replaced. The FBI has linked the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and about $3 billion has been frozen with help from Tether, Circle and Ripple.

An unknown investor has built a position in Zcash (ZEC) worth about $14 million, splitting the capital between the spot market and the decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid. The purchases came amid preparations for the Network Upgrade 7 (NU7) hard fork: on November 5, it is set to speed up block processing threefold.

Judging by on-chain data, the address t1JJnA linked to the investor first bought 3,052 ZEC (about $3.8 million) on the spot market at an average price of $1,250. Then, on Hyperliquid, it opened a 2x leveraged long on 8,000 ZEC worth $10.16 million in two different wallets.

So far, 3,000 ZEC of this position can be verified, with an average entry price of $1,353.83.

In late October, ZEC pulled back to the $1,220–$1,280 range, and the derivatives position went into the red. At its peak, the paper loss exceeded $1.8 million; it now stands at $249,388.

But liquidation will only occur if the price falls to $647.67, which is nearly half of current levels. The investor is clearly betting on long-term growth rather than a quick rebound.

The main argument is the NU7 hard fork, whose final tests the developers completed on the testnet in October. The ZIP-218 update will cut block time from 75 to 25 seconds: the network’s throughput will triple, while the issuance schedule will remain the same.

Along with the hard fork, the Network Sustainability Mechanism (a reserve fee fund for miners) will go live, and the outdated Sprout pool will be shut down in favor of the shielded Orchard architecture.

Justin Sun is seeking sanctions over World Liberty's delayed disclosure of UAE citizenship.

Sun says he'll pursue the case in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved.

The fight between Justin Sun and World Liberty Financial has taken another turn, this time over a disclosure that could affect where the case is heard. Sun is seeking sanctions against the Trump-linked crypto venture, alleging it disclosed its UAE citizenship months into their legal dispute. The Justin Sun sanctions motion adds a jurisdictional fight to an already messy dispute over frozen tokens and an alleged $45 million investment.

Sun sued World Liberty in April, accusing the project of fraud and unlawfully freezing his WLFI tokens. The company later countersued, describing his legal action as a “meritless PR stunt.”

The citizenship issue emerged after World Liberty amended its initial court disclosure. Its first filing reportedly listed one entity in its ownership chain and Florida as its sole citizenship. A subsequent filing identified 22 members in the ownership chain and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.

Sun argues the late UAE disclosure could undermine federal diversity jurisdiction, which depends on the parties having different citizenship for the case to proceed in federal court. He alleges the revised disclosure was an attempt to challenge that jurisdiction and move the dispute out of open court.

In a pointed post, Sun said World Liberty was “proudly American” when selling tokens, but discovered its UAE roots when it needed a way out of an American courtroom. He says he’ll refile in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved.

Sun says he invested $45 million in WLFI tokens. The token previously reached around $0.33 and now trades near $0.051, with a fully diluted valuation of approximately $5.1 billion.

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom. https://t.co/UIkyCfE0bS

The Justin Sun sanctions motion doesn’t settle the underlying token dispute. For now, the fight over ownership disclosures and court jurisdiction adds another complication to the case.

Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

Attackers reportedly compromised three Binance engineers before reaching the internal wallet signing service.

The timeline spans June, September and October, involving tampered software and a malicious code repository.

A claim blaming a Google ad has not been established by the preliminary investigation.

A major Binance hack didn’t begin with some sophisticated attack on the exchange’s front door. According to a preliminary investigation timeline, attackers compromised employees, stole credentials and eventually reached the platform’s internal wallet signing service.

The sequence raises uncomfortable questions about internal security. Three engineers became part of an attack chain that ultimately enabled unauthorized asset transfers.

The trouble reportedly started in June, when Wallet DevOps Engineer A downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer while configuring an AI coding tool. Binance detected the incident, replaced the device and rotated credentials. However, information about the engineer and colleagues had already been exposed.

Then came September. Engineer B downloaded a malicious code repository during what appeared to be a fake job interview, compromising his work computer.

Binance Hack Timeline: How Attackers Compromised Three Engineers to Access Wallet Signing ServiceWuBlockchain mapped the attack timeline based on Binance’s preliminary investigation. In June, Wallet DevOps Engineer A downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer while setting up an… pic.twitter.com/laEv7JMLBS

On October 20, attackers reportedly used the compromised device and an internal AI tool to gain control over Engineers A and C. They also discovered a container deployment permission token on Engineer A’s computer.

The operation escalated on October 29. Attackers accessed Engineer C’s device, used credentials stolen from A, deployed a container and executed a malicious script. That sequence ultimately enabled unauthorized transfers through Binance’s internal wallet signing service.

A separate commentator claimed the roughly $6 billion Binance hack resulted from a developer clicking a malicious Google advertisement, and argued Google should be held responsible.

However, the preliminary timeline does not establish that connection. It describes a tampered installer and a malicious repository, not a confirmed Google ad as the entry point.

Wow, turns out the $6 billion Binance hack was caused by a Binance developer clicking a malicious Google ad!I maintain my position: it's more important than ever to hold Google liable for platforming scams and turning a blind eye.Google was complicit in the Binance hack. https://t.co/RZwzjzdT9L pic.twitter.com/GhnFAQB1LM

The distinction matters. The Binance hack timeline points to compromised engineers, exposed credentials and deployment permissions as key parts of the attack. Blaming an advertising platform without evidence risks obscuring the specific security failures investigators are still examining.

Results of the 2026 US midterm elections will start coming in once the first polls close at 6pm Eastern Time on Tuesday, or 4:30am IST on Wednesday, beginning with parts of Indiana and Kentucky. Most of Florida, Georgia and Virginia close at 7pm ET (5:30am IST), and Pennsylvania, Maine and most of Michigan and Texas at 8pm ET (6:30am IST). Arizona, Iowa, Minnesota and Wisconsin close at 9pm ET (7:30am IST), California at 11pm ET (9:30am IST), and the last polls in western Alaska at 1am ET (11:30am IST). Early tallies are not final, because outlets such as the Associated Press call a race only when the margin is clear. Mail ballots and ranked-choice counting in Alaska, Maine, California, Nevada and Arizona could delay close races by days, so control of Congress may not be known on election night.

Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX, Netflix, SoFi Technologies and Lam Research have joined the list of companies rejecting OKX-ICE's plans.

OKX-ICE can still list tokenized shares directly issued or approved by the companies themselves.

OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are facing growing opposition to their plan to bring US stocks onto blockchain networks. Six more companies, including Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX and Netflix, have objected to having their shares tokenized on the proposed platform.

This brings the total number of objecting companies to 56 and puts nearly 80% of the platform’s planned stock selection at risk.

Can OKX and ICE still launch their tokenized stock platform?

The objections come as OKX and ICE prepare to offer tokenized versions of US stocks through a blockchain-based trading venue. The platform aims to let eligible users trade around the clock, using stablecoins such as USDC through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer network.

Supporters see tokenization as a way to make stock trading more accessible through longer trading hours and faster settlement.

However, companies may be concerned about how third-party tokens could affect their share prices, trading activity and reputation.

The objections do not completely shut down OKXICE’s plans. The venue can still offer tokenized shares issued or approved directly by the companies themselves, subject to applicable rules.

However, the growing list of objectors limits the selection of third-party tokenized stocks available to the platform. With 49 of its original 62 targets now opposing the proposed listings, OKXICE faces a major challenge in securing company participation.

The bigger question is whether the platform can attract enough issuers to make its planned 24/7 stock market viable.

#5278. Solana Officially Scores 1,000 Days Without Outage

The Solana network has hit a significant milestone in its quest to overcome its early hurdles, successfully going 1,000 days without a network-wide outage.

This feat stands in stark contrast to Solana's past, when the blockchain experienced some notable network disruptions. One of the more significant outages occurred in September 2021, when a spike in bot traffic from Grape Protocol IDO transactions led to a surge in transactions that overwhelmed validators and hindered consensus, resulting in a roughly 17-hour network outage.

The Solana network experienced similar problems in April 2022, with a large traffic spike due to an NFT mint that led to a roughly 7-hour outage. Another outage happened in June 2022, when a bug involving durable nonce transactions caused block production to stop for roughly 4.5 hours. Finally, in September 2022, the network experienced a fork due to a bug in the consensus layer, which led to a halt in block production lasting over 6 hours.

The final major outage occurred back in February 2023, when abnormal block forwarding overwhelmed Solana's Turbine block propagation system, leaving validators stuck in a vote-only state and leading to a coordinated restart. This would prove to be a monumental event for Solana in terms of its engineering progress.

Solana has seen a string of updates and engineering innovations by its developers in an effort to improve the network's ability to avoid the failures that had plagued it in the past. Some of these features include stake-weighted quality of service to better prioritize traffic from staked validators. The network also saw networking innovations such as QUIC that provide more flexibility in dealing with spam and congestion. There have also been updates to deduplication logic following the February 2023 outage. Additionally, the network has seen innovations such as a local fee market and other scheduling improvements to discourage users and bots from spamming the network with duplicate transactions.

Recently, Solana has emphasized that network resilience should be taken seriously. In a September 2026 update, the project shared that the network has seen 100% uptime since February 2024 and has continued to handle large amounts of traffic. It also highlighted a major infrastructure provider experiencing a routing failure in August 2026 that caused validators representing nearly 29% of the network's stake to go offline, but this did not result in a halt in block production. The project uses this as an example of increased fault tolerance.

For Solana, this 1,000-day milestone is not just a success in terms of network uptime. It's a statement and a demonstration to the world that a network once mocked for outages can now support serious financial and on-chain use cases.

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

DISCOVER: Meme coin supercycle: Top performers this week

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

EXPLORE: CZ Tells Crypto Users to Be “Extra Careful” Online as PHP Vulnerabilities Hit the Code Behind 70% of Websites: Can a Hacked Site Drain Your Wallet?

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.
